key_insight: CGMap uses distance-resolved graph learning to turn scattered cancer-related signals into an interpretable ranking of candidate genes. This helps researchers narrow their search and connect computational predictions to practical validation.
problem_solved: Cancer-related signals can be dispersed across gene networks, making it difficult to identify which genes deserve follow-up and explain why they were prioritized.
method: Use a distance-resolved graph-learning framework to organize cancer-related signals across a gene network.
Combine dispersed signals into structured priorities for candidate cancer genes.
Provide an interpretable path from gene-prioritization hypotheses to practical validation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, CGMap illustrates how graph learning can support interpretable scientific prioritization rather than predictions alone. Its intended value is to focus experimental follow-up on a smaller, more actionable set of candidates.
visual_elements: Gene-network diagram with distance bands showing signals at different network distances.
Workflow: dispersed cancer signals → CGMap → ranked candidate genes → validation.
Ranked gene list with highlighted candidates and visual links to supporting signals.
Funnel illustrating how prioritization narrows a broad candidate space.
paper_title: Interpretable distance-resolved graph learning for cancer gene priority screening
paper_authors: Chenhao Wang, Shidong Xu, Li Tang, Gang Luo, Yongchang Zhang
